# strfmt/fmt

> fmt(template, values...): a template with {} filled in by the values.

truck [strfmt](../strfmt.md) · [source](../../../registry/strfmt/fmt.pkg)

```
print fmt("{} is {} years old", "Ada", 36)     // Ada is 36 years old
print fmt("[{:5}] [{:-5}] [{:05}]", 42, 42, -42)
// [   42] [42   ] [-0042]
print fmt("{{}} stays")                         // {} stays
```

Each `{}` takes the next value, shown as text with `show`, so a value
can be an `int`, `str`, `bool`, `u8`, `[int]` or `[str]`.

| placeholder | gives |
|---|---|
| `{}` | the value |
| `{:N}` | right-aligned in `N` columns (bytes) |
| `{:-N}` | left-aligned in `N` columns |
| `{:0N}` | right-aligned, padded with zeros after any sign |
| `{{`, `}}` | a literal `{` or `}` |

A `{}` without a value becomes `{!missing}`, a value without a `{}` is
added as `{!extra value}`, and an unknown spec as `{!bad spec}`, so
mistakes show in the output. The template can be any `str` expression;
for values that are already strings in a vector, use `sf_format`.

## Syntax

Kind: `expr`

```
fmt ( {t: expr str} [ , {x: expr any} ]* ) -> str
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `t` | expression | `str` |
| `x` (optional) | expression | `any` |

Produces: `str`
